questions.question: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mini Constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, is widely referred to as the **Mini Constitution** because it introduced the most extensive and sweeping changes to the **Constitution of India** since its adoption in **1950**.
 
• It was enacted during the **National Emergency** (1975−1977) under the leadership of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**, following the recommendations submitted by the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
• This amendment uniquely modified the **Preamble** of the Constitution by inserting three new terms: **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity**.
 
• It added **Part IV-A** to the Constitution, which established a set of **ten Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens under **Article 51A**.
 
• The act sought to establish the supremacy of the **Parliament** by limiting the power of the **Judiciary** to review constitutional amendments and restricting the **High Courts'** power to issue writs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legislative and Executive Changes**:

 
 
• Five key subjects were transferred from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**: **Education**, **Forests**, **Weights and Measures**, **Protection of Wild Animals and Birds**, and **Administration of Justice**.
 
• The tenure of the **Lok Sabha** and the **State Legislative Assemblies** was extended from **5 years to 6 years**.
 
• It made it mandatory for the **President** to act in accordance with the advice of the **Council of Ministers**.
 
 
 
• **New Directive Principles**:
 
 
• Three new **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** were added: **Article 39A** (Equal justice and free legal aid), **Article 43A** (Participation of workers in management), and **Article 48A** (Protection and improvement of environment).
 
• Most of the controversial provisions of this amendment were later repealed or modified by the **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978**, to restore democratic checks and balances.

questions.question: What is the standard duration of a women's kabaddi match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15 min per half**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The standard duration of a **women's kabaddi match** is strictly governed by the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)** and the **Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI)**, consisting of **two halves of 15 minutes** each.
 
• There is a designated **5-minute interval** between the two halves, allowing players to rest and teams to switch their respective sides of the court.
 
• This **30-minute total play time** (excluding the break) is also applied to matches for **junior girls**, **sub-junior girls**, and **sub-junior boys** to account for physical endurance requirements.
 
• Each **raid** during the match is restricted to a maximum of **30 seconds**, a rule enforced by the **technical officials** to maintain the high-paced nature of the sport.
 
• In the event of a tie during knockout stages, extra time may be played, typically consisting of **two halves of 7 minutes** each with a **3-minute break**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Comparison with Men's Kabaddi:
 
 
• In the **senior men** and **junior boys** categories, the match duration is longer, totaling **40 minutes** of play divided into **two halves of 20 minutes** each.
 
 
 
• Court Dimensions and Weight Limits:
 
 
• The **playing court** for women measures **12 meters × 8 meters**, which is smaller than the men's court of **13 meters × 10 meters**.
 
• For official national and international championships, **senior women** participants must typically adhere to a maximum **weight limit of 75 kg**.
 
 
 
• Team Composition:
 
 
• Each team consists of **12 players**, but only **7 players** take the field at any given time, with **5 substitutes** held in reserve.
 
• A team earns **2 bonus points** (known as **Lona**) when they successfully declare the entire opposing team **out**.

questions.question: In what year was the Khalsa established by Guru Gobind Singh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1699**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Khalsa**, which refers to the community of initiated Sikhs, was established by **Guru Gobind Singh Ji**, the tenth and final human Guru of Sikhism.
 
• This historic event took place on the day of **Vaisakhi**, specifically on **April 13, 1699** (or April 14 in some calendars), at **Anandpur Sahib** in **Punjab**.
 
• During this assembly, the Guru called for five volunteers who were willing to give their heads for the faith, leading to the creation of the **Panj Pyare** (Five Beloved Ones).
 
• The formation of the Khalsa was a transformative moment that shifted the Sikh community into a disciplined order of **Saint-Soldiers** to fight against the religious persecution of the **Mughal Empire**.
 
• The Guru introduced the **Amrit Sanchar** (initiation ceremony) where sugar crystals were stirred in water with a **Khanda** (double-edged sword) to create **Amrit** (nectar).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Gobind Singh**:

 
 
• He was born in **Patna** in 1666 and became the Guru at the age of nine after the martyrdom of his father, **Guru Tegh Bahadur**.
 
• He codified the Sikh way of life and eventually declared the **Guru Granth Sahib** as the eternal living Guru for all Sikhs.
 
 
 
• **The Five Ks (Panj Kakar)**:
 
 
• Members of the Khalsa are required to wear five articles of faith: **Kesh** (uncut hair), **Kangha** (wooden comb), **Kara** (iron bracelet), **Kachera** (cotton undergarments), and **Kirpan** (steel sword).
 
• These symbols were intended to give Sikhs a **distinct identity** and a constant reminder of their spiritual and social duties.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Name**:
 
 
• The term **Khalsa** is derived from the Arabic word **khalis**, meaning 'pure' or 'free from impurities'.
 
• Upon initiation, men were given the title **Singh** (Lion) and women were given the title **Kaur** (Princess), symbolizing the **abolition of caste** hierarchies and gender inequality.

questions.question: In July 2025, which state government launched the Digi-Lakshmi scheme to digitally empower urban poor women?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 2025**, the state government of **Andhra Pradesh** launched the **Digi-Lakshmi** scheme as a dedicated effort toward the **digital empowerment** of **urban poor women**.
 
• The initiative primarily targets women organized under **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** within urban local bodies to enhance their **technological proficiency**.
 
• The scheme provides beneficiaries with **smartphones** and **subsidized data plans**, ensuring they have the necessary hardware to participate in the **digital economy**.
 
• A core objective of **Digi-Lakshmi** is to facilitate **financial inclusion** by training women in **digital banking**, **UPI transactions**, and the use of **government service portals**.
 
• The program aims to foster **entrepreneurship** among women, allowing them to access **online marketplaces** and expand the reach of their small-scale businesses beyond local physical markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nodal Agency and Framework**:

 
 
• The **Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas (MEPMA)** serves as the lead agency for identifying beneficiaries and monitoring the implementation of the **Digi-Lakshmi** project.
 
• This scheme complements **Andhra Pradesh**'s existing welfare architecture, which includes the **Navaratnalu** programs aimed at **poverty alleviation** and **women's welfare**.
 
 
 
• **Digital Literacy Training**:
 
 
• Beneficiaries receive hands-on training in **cyber security** and **safe digital practices** to protect them from financial fraud and online exploitation.
 
• The training includes modules on **e-commerce logistics** and **digital marketing** via social media platforms to help women-led micro-enterprises scale effectively.
 
 
 
• **Wider Policy Alignment**:
 
 
• The scheme aligns with the national **Digital India** mission, specifically addressing the **gender digital divide** that often limits women's economic opportunities in developing urban clusters.
 
• It streamlines the delivery of **Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT)**, ensuring that government subsidies reach the bank accounts of women without the need for middlemen.

questions.question:
Which of the following factor controls the climate of any place?

I. Ocean current 

II. Relief feature
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ocean currents** significantly influence the temperature and moisture levels of coastal regions. Any coastal area with warm or cold currents flowing past it will be warmed or cooled if the winds are **onshore**. For example, the **North Atlantic Drift** keeps Western European ports ice-free in winter, while cold currents can lead to the formation of coastal deserts like the **Atacama**. Hence, statement I is correct.
 
• **Relief features** refer to the physical layout of the land, such as mountains, plateaus, and plains, which act as major climate controls. High mountains function as barriers for cold or hot winds and force moist air to rise, leading to **orographic precipitation**. The **windward side** of a mountain range receives heavy rainfall, whereas the **leeward side** remains dry, creating a **rain shadow region**. Hence, statement II is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are six major controls of the climate of any place:
 
 
• **Latitude**: The amount of solar energy received varies according to the distance from the **Equator**, causing temperatures to generally decrease from the equator toward the poles.
 
• **Altitude**: As one moves to higher elevations, the atmosphere becomes less dense and the temperature decreases, which is why mountains are cooler than plains during summer.
 
• **Pressure and Wind System**: This depends on the latitude and altitude of a place and influences the **temperature** and **rainfall** patterns.
 
• **Distance from the Sea**: The sea exerts a moderating influence on climate. As the distance from the sea increases, this influence decreases, leading to **extreme weather conditions** known as **continentality**.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a type of projects covered under SHRESHTA Scheme?

I. Residential Schools

II. Non-Residential Schools
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **SHRESHTA** scheme, or the **Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas**, was initiated by the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** to uplift students from the **Scheduled Caste (SC)** communities.
 
• The scheme is implemented through two distinct modes: **Mode 1** facilitates admission into reputed private **Residential Schools** via a national entrance test, and **Mode 2** provides financial grants to **Voluntary Organizations (VOs)** or NGOs.
 
• Under the **Grant-in-Aid** component for NGOs, the government specifically funds the operation of **Residential Schools** (up to class 12) to provide holistic educational environments for SC students. Hence, statement I is correct.
 
• The same component also covers and provides financial support for the maintenance of **Non-Residential Schools** and **Hostels**, ensuring that quality education reaches students even in non-boarding setups. Hence, statement II is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The scheme targets meritorious **SC students** whose parental annual income is up to **Rs. 2.5 lakh**.
 
• Key features of the implementation include:
 
 
• Selection through the **National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS)**, which is conducted by the **National Testing Agency (NTA)**.
 
• Focus on classes **9th and 11th** for direct admission into private schools affiliated with the **CBSE** or State Boards.
 
• Provision of a **Bridge Course** within the schools to help students adapt to the new academic environment for the first three months.
 
• The **Department of Social Justice and Empowerment** bears the total expenditure, including **school fees**, **hostel fees**, and other academic costs.

questions.question: Which of the following article of the Indian constitution deals with Official language of the Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 343**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 343(1)** of the **Indian Constitution** explicitly declares that the **Official Language** of the **Union** shall be **Hindi** in **Devanagari script**.
 
• The article specifies that the form of **numerals** to be used for the official purposes of the **Union** shall be the **international form of Indian numerals**, rather than the **Devanagari** form.
 
• According to **Article 343(2)**, for a period of **fifteen years** from the commencement of the **Constitution** (until 1965), the **English language** was permitted to continue being used for all **official purposes** of the **Union** for which it was being used before.
 
• **Article 343(3)** empowers the **Parliament** to provide by law for the continued use of the **English language** or the **Devanagari form of numerals** for specified purposes even after the initial **fifteen-year** period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 341**:

 
 
• This article pertains to **Scheduled Castes**. It authorizes the **President** to specify the castes, races, or tribes which shall be deemed as Scheduled Castes in relation to a **State** or **Union Territory**.
 
 
 
• **Article 344**:
 
 
• It provides for the constitution of a **Commission** and a **Committee of Parliament** on **Official Language** to make recommendations to the **President** regarding the progressive use of the **Hindi language**.
 
 
 
• **Article 339**:
 
 
• This article deals with the **Union Government’s** control over the administration of **Scheduled Areas** and the welfare of **Scheduled Tribes**.
 
 
 
• **Part XVII**:
 
 
• The provisions related to the **Official Language** are contained in **Part XVII** of the **Constitution**, covering **Articles 343 to 351**. This includes **Regional Languages**, **Language of the Supreme Court**, and **Special Directives** for language development.

questions.question: The classical dance form 'Kathakali' is associated with which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathakali** is one of the eight major **classical dances** of India, originating from the southwestern state of **Kerala** during the **17th century**.
 
• The dance form is a unique combination of literature, music, painting, acting, and dance, often referred to as **'total theater'**.
 
• It is traditionally performed by male actors who depict stories from Indian epics like the **Ramayana**, **Mahabharata**, and the **Puranas**.
 
• The performance is renowned for its **elaborate makeup**, **heavy costumes**, and **grand headgear**, where facial colors signify character traits: **Green (Pacha)** for noble characters and **Red/Black** for evil or demonic ones.
 
• A crucial element of Kathakali is the use of **24 basic Mudras** (hand gestures) and **9 Navarasas** (facial expressions) to convey emotions and narrative without speech.
 
• Musical accompaniment includes the **Chenda**, **Maddalam**, and **Elathalam**, while the singing follows the **Sopanam** tradition of **Kerala**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sikkim**:

 
 
• Known for folk dances such as the **Singhi Chaam** (Snow Lion Dance) and **Yak Chaam**, which are deeply rooted in **Tibetan Buddhist** traditions.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra**:
 
 
• The state is famous for **Lavani**, a vibrant folk dance performed to the rhythmic beats of the **Dholki**, and **Koli**, the traditional dance of the fishing community.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**:
 
 
• Renowned for **Garba** and **Dandiya Raas**, which are celebratory folk dances performed primarily during the **Navratri** festival.
 
• **Bhavai** is a popular folk theater form native to this state.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Kerala**

questions.question: Which traditional Rajasthani instrument is a long bronze trumpet made in two parts with a funnel-shaped opening?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Turhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Turhi** is a traditional **Rajasthani aerophone** (wind instrument) primarily used in **folk music**, processions, and religious ceremonies.
 
• It is a long, straight **trumpet-like instrument** traditionally crafted from metals such as **bronze** or **brass** to ensure high sound resonance and environmental durability.
 
• A distinctive structural feature of the **Turhi** is its construction in **two separate parts** or segments that are fitted together, which facilitates easier transport and maintenance.
 
• The instrument terminates in a wide, **funnel-shaped opening** or bell, which helps in projecting a loud, clear, and commanding sound suitable for **open-air performances**.
 
• Historically, the **Turhi** was played by professional folk musicians to herald the arrival of **Maharajas**, lead **martial processions**, and announce the start of major festivals like **Gangaur** and **Teej**.
 
• In the classification of Indian musical instruments, it falls under the **Sushira Vadya** category, which produces sound through the vibration of a column of air.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Timki**:

 
 
• This is a small **percussion instrument** or kettle drum (Avanaddha Vadya) commonly played by the **Bhil** and **Garasia** tribes of **Rajasthan** and **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It is often played with wooden sticks to provide a rhythmic base for community folk dances and tribal songs.
 
 
 
• **Sarod**:
 
 
• A prominent **stringed instrument** (Tata Vadya) of the **Hindustani classical** tradition, recognized for its deep and resonant timbre.
 
• It features a **fretless metal fingerboard**, allowing musicians to perform smooth glides between notes, a technique essential to Indian ragas.
 
 
 
• **Santoor**:
 
 
• A traditional **hammered dulcimer** with ancient roots, specifically associated with the **Kashmir Valley** and its **Sufiana Mausiqi**.
 
• It consists of a trapezoidal wooden box with over **72 strings** that are struck with delicate wooden mallets called **Kalam**.

questions.question: Kabaddi game is primarily known as "Hu-Tu-Tu" in ___ India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kabaddi** is a highly popular indigenous contact sport in India that requires both physical strength and tactical skills, played between two teams of seven players each.
 
• In **Western India**, particularly in the state of **Maharashtra**, the game has been traditionally and primarily known as **Hu-Tu-Tu**.
 
• The term **Hu-Tu-Tu** refers to the continuous rhythmic chant or cant maintained by the raider to demonstrate they are holding their breath while in the opponent's territory.
 
• The formalization of the **Western** style of the game began in the early 20th century, with clubs like the **Deccan Gymkhana** in **Pune** drafting the first set of standardized rules in **1918**.
 
• The **All India Kabaddi Federation** was established in **1950**, which helped merge various regional styles like **Hu-Tu-Tu** into a unified national competitive format.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Regional Nomenclature of Kabaddi:
 
 
• **Southern India**: In states like **Tamil Nadu**, **Karnataka**, and **Andhra Pradesh**, the game is commonly referred to as **Chedugudu** or **Gudu-gudu**.
 
• **Eastern India**: In **West Bengal** and the neighboring country of **Bangladesh**, it is famously known as **Ha-du-du**.
 
• **Northern India**: The sport is predominantly known by its standard name, **Kabaddi**, or sometimes as **Kaun-bada**.
 
 
 
• Major Milestones and Governance:
 
 
• The **Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI)** was founded in **1972** and is the primary governing body for the sport in the country.
 
• The **Hanuman Vyayam Prasarak Mandal** from **Amaravati**, Maharashtra, showcased the sport at the **1936 Berlin Olympics** as a demonstration event.
 
• Kabaddi was officially included as a medal sport in the **Asian Games** for the first time during the **11th Asian Games** held in **Beijing** in **1990**.
 
• It is recognized as the **National Sport** of **Bangladesh** and the state sport of several Indian states, including **Maharashtra**, **Punjab**, and **Tamil Nadu**.

questions.question: Which of the following sports has not yet given India a gold medal at the Asian Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weightlifting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Weightlifting** has seen Indian athletes achieve major success at the **Olympics** and **Commonwealth Games**, but the sport has not yet yielded a **Gold medal** for India at the **Asian Games**. Since the inaugural games in **1951**, India has won several silver and bronze medals, but the top podium finish remains elusive. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Shooting** has been a highly successful discipline for India, with the first individual gold medal won by **Randhir Singh** in **1978** at the **Bangkok Asian Games**. Since then, shooters like **Jaspal Rana** and **Saurabh Chaudhary** have added numerous gold medals to India's tally. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Golf** gave India its first set of gold medals during the **1982 Asian Games** held in **New Delhi**. **Laxman Singh** won the individual gold, and the **Indian Men's team** also secured the gold medal in the team event. **Shiv Kapur** further added a gold medal in **2002**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Athletics** is the most prolific sport for India at the **Asian Games**, contributing the highest number of gold medals. Legends such as **Milkha Singh**, **P.T. Usha**, and more recently, **Neeraj Chopra** in the javelin throw, have consistently won gold for the country. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weightlifting Performance**:

 
 
• **Karnam Malleswari** won silver medals in the **1994 Hiroshima** and **1998 Bangkok** editions.
 
• **N. Kunjarani Devi** secured bronze medals in **1990** and **1994**, while **Mirabai Chanu** has yet to win a gold at this specific event.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• In the **1951 Asian Games**, India's first-ever gold medal was won by **Sachin Nag** in **Swimming**, but the track and field events (**Athletics**) quickly became India's strongest domain.
 
• The **2022 Hangzhou Asian Games** (held in 2023) saw India crossing the **100-medal mark** for the first time, with **Shooting** and **Athletics** being the primary contributors to the gold medal count.
